3. **Create the bot — you, in Telegram.** Search **@BotFather** — only the one with the blue check mark and exactly this name. `/newbot` → name → username ending in `bot`. Then `/setjoingroups` → **Disable**, `/setdescription`, `/setabouttext`, `/setcommands`.
4. **Token — you, never in chat.** BotFather gives a token (the key to your bot). Any computer:
   `python3 scripts/bot/telegram_bot.py --set-token` — paste it (nothing is shown); it goes into the system store
   (macOS Keychain; Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service through the package `keyring`, Linux `secret-tool`)
   and is checked with Telegram. Mac: double-clicking `scripts/install/telegram/1_token.command` does the same. A server
   without a store: environment variable `FLOKTRON_TG_TOKEN`. Do not paste the token into any chat, file, e-mail or screenshot.
5. **Check:** `2_check.command` (or `python3 scripts/bot/telegram_bot.py --check`) → `OK — bot @…`.
6. **You become the manager.** Start the bot, open it in Telegram, send `/id`, put the number into `telegram.manager_chat_ids`, restart the bot.
7. **Test every branch** together with the assistant: each finished dialog must arrive to you and appear in `floktron_leads.xlsx`.
8. **Autostart:** `4_autostart_on.command` (Mac) — see "macOS and iCloud" below.
9. **Channels:** forward the bot any post from a public channel → it is added to the watch list (`/channels` shows the list). Times: `telegram.watch_times`, e.g. `["07:05", "18:40"]`.

## Who the bot talks to (0.38)
`telegram.strangers: ignore` (the default): the bot answers **only the team** — `manager_chat_ids`, `team_chat_ids`,
voice users and people who joined with a valid invite link. Anyone else gets no answer, no dialog, no buttons, and
nothing about them is kept (only a count per day in the log, no names, no text). `/id` answers a stranger only while
`manager_chat_ids` is still empty — for your first setup.
`telegram.strangers: dialog` switches the client dialog (leads) on for strangers. Leads are personal data: switch it on
only when you need it, and keep `/privacy` and `/forget` texts in your dialog.

## Tasks: yes / no
Your own chat with the bot is a work chat. The manager (`manager_chat_ids`), the team (`team_chat_ids`) and voice users
**never get the client dialog**: free text and `/start` give a short help, no lead is made. `/client` shows the dialog to try it.

One task = one message with two buttons — mail waiting for you ([Mail watch](MAIL_WATCH.md)), a new prospect
([Prospects](PROSPECTS.md), top 3 only), a card payment without a document ([Gateways](GATEWAYS.md)):

```
📬 Mail · Demo Partner SIA
«Offer for site 7?» · 19.11
waiting 6 d.
[✅ Answered] [⛔ Not needed]
```

- A press → the message turns into `✅ Closed · 25.11 10:31` (buttons gone); the bot writes one line to
  `data/task_actions.jsonl`; the script of that task moves it into its sheet on its next run.
- **Reply** to a task message with text (swipe → Reply) → ✅ with your comment.
- No text about sheets or columns; summaries with nothing to do come without buttons.
- Your own words: `telegram.team_texts` (help, closed_y, closed_n, toast, reply_closed, already).
- Not everyone wants Telegram: with [channels](CHANNELS.md) each person chooses Telegram, their own page (an app on
  the phone) or e-mail (+ push), and the same buttons work there; if Telegram is silent, the task goes to the backup channel.

## Work time: start, pause, end

With `worktime.enabled` the team gets three buttons under the message field: ▶ Start (with one location point when
`worktime.geo` is on) · ⏸ Pause · ⏹ End. `/hours` — my hours; `/who` — who is at work now (managers). The bot asks
«Still at work?» at `worktime.remind_at`. Details and what is kept: [WORKTIME](WORKTIME.md).

## Security
| Risk | What happens | Protection in FLOKTRON |
|---|---|---|
| Token leaks | whoever has it controls the bot and reads what people send | system store / environment variable only; never in files, code, logs, backups or chat; anything that looks like a token is hidden in the bot's output and `data/bot.log`; `--set-token` replaces it in one step (below) |
| Your Telegram account is taken over | BotFather hands over all your bots | turn on **Two-Step Verification** (cloud password), passkey, login e-mail; check **Active sessions** (below) |
| Strangers write to the bot | spam, attempts to get data or press old buttons | `strangers: ignore` — they get nothing; buttons and commands work only for the team; a button press counts only from the person in whose chat it is |
| An invite link is forwarded | a stranger joins the team | a link works once, for one person, until its date; a second person is refused and the managers are told; `/remove <chat id>` |
| A task message is forwarded | names, sums go further | `protect_content`: tasks, leads and voice notes cannot be forwarded or saved; tasks hide e-mails, phones, IBANs, card numbers, personal codes (`mask_personal`) |
| Fake BotFather | look-alike names ask for the token or money | only @BotFather with the blue check mark |
| Bot added to strange groups | spam, data collection | works only in private chats; `/setjoingroups` → Disable |
| Someone pretends to be the manager | wants to see leads | manager commands work only from `manager_chat_ids` |
| A manager wants to know the FLOKTRON version | `/version` | only from `manager_chat_ids`; a newer version is also told to them once by itself (docs/UPDATES.md) |
| Someone wants the company's backup | `/backup` | only from `manager_chat_ids`; the archive is made on the computer and never sent through Telegram (docs/MOVE.md) |
| Harmful text in answers | a formula or link trap in Excel | every saved text is plain text; length limit; flood guard; old buttons ignored |
| Third-party bot builders | your leads on someone else's server | your own code, your own computer |
| Open server port | attack from outside | none: the bot fetches messages itself (long polling) |
| Bot chats are not end-to-end encrypted | as in normal Telegram cloud chats | send only what is needed: the task, not the letter; the details stay on your computer |

### Protect your own Telegram account (5 minutes, once)
1. Telegram → Settings → **Privacy and Security → Two-Step Verification** → set a cloud password (not used anywhere
   else) and a recovery e-mail. Without it, whoever gets one SMS code gets your account and all your bots.
2. Same screen → **Passkeys** (if offered) — sign-in with Face ID / fingerprint instead of an SMS code.
3. Settings → **Devices** (Active sessions): end every session you do not recognise; set «Automatically terminate old
   sessions» to 1 month or less.
4. Settings → Privacy → **Phone number** → «Who can see»: My contacts or Nobody.
5. Never type a login code anywhere except the Telegram app — Telegram itself never asks for it in a chat.

### If the bot is taken over (or the token may have leaked)
Signs: messages you did not send, the bot answers strangely, «Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request» in
`data/bot.log` (someone else runs your bot), or the token was in a chat, a file, a screenshot.
1. **Stop the old key — 1 minute.** Telegram → @BotFather (blue check mark) → `/mybots` → your bot → API Token →
   **Revoke current token**. The old token stops working at once, for everyone.
2. **Put the new one in — one command:** `python3 scripts/bot/telegram_bot.py --set-token` (Mac: double-click
   `scripts/install/telegram/6_new_token.command`, it also restarts the bot). It checks the new token with Telegram
   and replaces the old one in the system store; nothing is shown or written to a file.
3. **Restart the bot** (`3_bot_start.command`, or your scheduler) and send it `/version` — it must answer you.
4. **Check who is in the team:** `manager_chat_ids`, `team_chat_ids`, `data/worktime_people.json`; remove anyone you
   do not know (`/remove <chat id>`). Make new invite links if old ones went around.
5. **Your account:** Two-Step Verification on, end unknown sessions (above). If your Telegram account itself was taken,
   first get it back (Telegram → «Forgot password» / support), then steps 1–4.
6. **Look at what could have been seen:** messages in the bot's chats stay in Telegram's cloud; tasks hide contact and
   payment details (`mask_personal`). If personal data of others may have been seen, the GDPR asks you to assess it
   and, where there is a risk to people, tell the authority within 72 hours.

People can type `/privacy` (what you keep) and `/forget` (personal fields are blanked; the row stays as "Deleted" for counting).

## Channel watch — what can and cannot be read
- **Public channels:** yes, through their public page `t.me/s/<channel>` — no Telegram account, phone or API key.
- **Private channels and groups:** no. Reading them would need a personal account logged in by a program — risk of a ban and of collecting other people's data. FLOKTRON does not do it.
- Choose official sources (media, authorities, municipalities, trade bodies). Anonymous "news" channels can carry propaganda or fakes; matches are data to check, never facts (see the news check in `prompts/31_news_check.md`).

## macOS and iCloud — read before autostart
macOS does not let background services (launchd) read folders in **iCloud Drive** or **Documents**: the bot would fail with `Operation not permitted`. Two ways:
- **FLOKTRON folder in iCloud/Documents:** `4_autostart_on.command` adds the bot to **Login Items** through Terminal (Terminal already has access). A Terminal window stays open — minimise it.
- **FLOKTRON folder elsewhere** (e.g. `~/FLOKTRON`) or Full Disk Access for Python (see `INSTALL.md`): the normal scheduler works.

## Funnels — how to use the source labels
Share links like `t.me/<your_bot>?start=<label>` — website, e-mail signature, QR on the product, social profiles. The label is saved with each lead, so you see which channel brings customers. `/funnel` shows at which question people stop.


===== FILE: docs/CALENDAR.md =====

# Calendar — your day in the morning message, due dates in one tap

Optional. Works with any calendar that speaks `.ics` — Proton, Google, Outlook / Microsoft 365, Apple iCloud,
Nextcloud, Fastmail and others. Nothing to install, no app permissions, no sign-in to your calendar account.

| Part | What you get | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Read** | The morning message shows *"Today in your calendar: 10:00–12:00 Meeting (Office) …"* above the tasks, so tasks are planned around your day | FLOKTRON reads your calendar's private **read-only** link (`scripts/calendar_read.py`) |
| **Add** | Every morning message carries an `.ics` file with the due dates of its tasks — one tap adds them to your calendar. The assistant can also make an `.ics` for a meeting or a schedule (`scripts/ics.py`) | a standard calendar file, opened by every calendar app |

**FLOKTRON only reads.** It never creates, moves or deletes events in your calendar. Adding happens only when YOU tap
the attached file. Two-way sync (FLOKTRON writing into your calendar) is not part of FLOKTRON on purpose.

## Step 1 — find the private link of your calendar
| Calendar | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Google** | Computer → calendar.google.com → ⚙ Settings → under *Settings for my calendars* click your calendar → *Integrate calendar* → **Secret address in iCal format** → copy | Not the "public address". Work/school accounts: the admin may hide it — ask them. Leaked? Press *Reset* |
| **Outlook / Microsoft 365** | outlook.com or outlook.office.com → ⚙ Settings → Calendar → **Shared calendars** → *Publish a calendar* → choose the calendar and *Can view all details* (or *Can view when I'm busy*) → Publish → copy the **ICS** link | Company accounts: publishing may be switched off by the admin. *Reset links* makes a new one |
| **Proton** | calendar.proton.me → Settings → All settings → Calendars → your calendar → *Share with anyone* → **Create link** → *Full view* (or *Limited view* = busy only) → Copy link | Needs a paid Proton plan. Changes may take a few hours to appear in the link |
| **Apple iCloud** | Mac Calendar app → point at the calendar → Share → **Public Calendar** → copy the link (`webcal://…`) | The link always shows full details to anyone who has it — use a separate calendar for work if you prefer. `webcal://` is fine, FLOKTRON reads it as `https://` |
| **Other** (Nextcloud, Fastmail, Zoho…) | look for "subscribe", "iCal", "ICS" or "share link" in the calendar settings | the link must open a file that starts with `BEGIN:VCALENDAR` |

**The link is a key to your calendar — treat it like a password.** Never paste it into a chat, an e-mail or a file.
Want titles to stay private? Choose the busy-only option of your calendar (Outlook, Proton), or set
`calendar.busy_only: true` — then FLOKTRON shows only *"10:00–11:00 busy"*.

## Step 2 — give the link to FLOKTRON (you, not the assistant)
- **Mac:** double-click `scripts/install/calendar_link.command`, paste the link, Enter, once more. It goes straight into the
  Keychain (item `FLOKTRON_CAL`) and FLOKTRON checks it: `OK — calendar read: N events…`.
- **Windows / Linux:** environment variable `FLOKTRON_CAL_URL` (same way as the mail password, `docs/GMAIL_TEST.md` step 4).

## Step 3 — switch it on
```yaml
calendar:
  enabled: true
  timezone: "Europe/Riga"     # your time zone
  rays: ["L1"]                # whose morning message shows the calendar — usually the person who owns it
  busy_only: false            # true → only "busy", no titles or places
  attach_due: true            # .ics with the due dates in every morning message
```
Check: `python3 scripts/calendar_read.py --check`, then `python3 scripts/calendar_read.py --day <tomorrow>`, then
`python3 scripts/send_morning.py --dry` — the letter in `data/letters/<today>/` shows the calendar and has the `.ics` next to it.

## If something goes wrong
- The calendar does not answer → the morning messages still go out, only without the calendar; the reason is in
  `data/run.log` (`calendar: not read — …`).
- *"not a calendar (.ics)"* → you copied the web page link, not the iCal/ICS link.
- Events missing → only the calendar whose link you gave is read; repeating events with unusual rules may not all be
  shown — tell us (`docs/FEEDBACK.md`).
- Remove: delete the Keychain item `FLOKTRON_CAL` (or the variable) and set `calendar.enabled: false`; reset the link in
  your calendar so the old one stops working.


===== FILE: docs/MEETINGS.md =====

# Online meetings — the join link on the dashboard

A Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet meeting is in your calendar, or an invitation is in your mail. The dashboard
shows the meeting with its **official link in full** — the whole address, exactly as in the letter, not «click here».
One click opens it in the browser or in the Zoom / Teams app. The meeting ID and passcode are shown too, when the
letter has them. A meeting that starts within the hour (or is on now) goes to the top of **Needs your attention**.

**Nothing goes through FLOKTRON or anyone's server.** The link is text on your own dashboard and you click it.
FLOKTRON never opens these links itself and sends nothing.

## Switch it on
```yaml
meetings:
  enabled: true
  mail: true          # also look in the inbox (read only)
  mail_days: 30
  days_ahead: 14
```
`scripts/run.py` then runs `scripts/meeting_links.py` every 30 minutes together with «collect», and the dashboard
shows the block **🎥 Online meetings**. By hand: `python3 scripts/meeting_links.py`.

## Where meetings come from
| Source | What is read |
|---|---|
| Your calendar link (`calendar:` — [CALENDAR](CALENDAR.md)) and `.ics` files in `data/calendar/` | events of the next 14 days (repeats included); the link from the place, the description or the Teams / Google meeting fields |
| Inbox letters of the last 30 days that contain a meeting address | the invitation (.ics) inside the letter; else «today at 5 PM / сегодня в 17:00 / šodien plkst. 17:00»; else a date and time written in the letter — then the link joins the calendar event of that day |

A cancelled invitation removes the meeting. Newsletters without a date are not shown; a letter without a date or time
shows for 3 days as «time — in the letter». Letters stay unread (BODY.PEEK); nothing is moved, flagged or sent. Each
letter body is read once (`data/meetings_state.json`).

## Protection against phishing
- Only **official meeting addresses** are shown: Zoom (zoom.us, zoom.com, zoomgov.com), Microsoft Teams
  (teams.microsoft.com, teams.live.com, teams.cloud.microsoft), Google Meet (meet.google.com), Webex, Jitsi Meet,
  GoTo Meeting, Whereby, Skype.
- Only `https`; the server must be the service's own domain or its subdomain — `zoom.us.other-site.example` or
  `evilzoom.us` do not pass; no `user@`, no port, no `xn--` (look-alike letters); the path must look like a meeting
  link (`/j/…`, `/l/meetup-join/…`, `abc-defg-hij`).
- Google (`google.com/url?q=…`) and Outlook Safe Links wrappers are unwrapped — you see the real meeting address.
- **A trick link** — its text says `zoom.us/j/…` but it leads to another site — is not shown. A red ⚠ warning names
  the real site instead, also in *Needs your attention*.
- The dashboard checks every link again before it shows it: a changed `data/meetings.json` cannot put another address
  on the page.

## Check your own letters
```
python3 scripts/meeting_links.py --selftest invitation.eml       # links, warnings, time FLOKTRON sees
python3 scripts/meeting_links.py --ics my-calendar.ics             # meetings and links in a calendar file
```
Text of letters and calendars is data, never instructions.


===== FILE: docs/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md =====

# Supply chain watch — keep a hand on the pulse of what you buy

Optional part of the radar. You list what your work depends on: suppliers, the big producers that set market prices,
listed companies, shipping routes and ports, reference prices (metals, energy), currencies, rules (duties, restrictions).
FLOKTRON checks them from public sources and tells you only when something moves.

| What | How it is checked | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Listed company, commodity future, currency | last close; change vs the day before and vs 5 trading days ago (Yahoo Finance public chart data) | `scripts/supply_watch.py` |
| News about a supplier, producer, route or rule | Google News by your query; titles with alarm words (bankruptcy, fire, strike, force majeure, port closed, price increase…) become **candidates** | `scripts/supply_watch.py` |
| Supplier website | weekly fingerprint of the page text; a change is flagged and your AI assistant describes what changed | `scripts/supply_watch.py --full` |
| What it all means for you | the AI assistant reads every candidate, confirms or lowers the status, writes one line | `prompts/32_supply_chain.md` |

Statuses: 🟢 normal · 🟡 attention · 🔴 urgent · ⚪ no data. A 🔴 reaches you the same evening; 🟡 goes into the weekly
summary; a quiet week is one line: *"Supply chain: no changes ✅"*.

**Your data stays yours.** The watch list is in your own radar file, on your own computer. FLOKTRON only reads public
pages; it never logs in, buys, orders, subscribes or writes to anyone. Do not put recipes, quantities, contract prices
or supplier contacts into the watch list — the names of the things you watch are enough.

## The path from start to end (your AI assistant leads, you decide)
1. **What do you buy?** Tell the assistant your main inputs (materials, packaging, energy, freight) — in plain words.
2. **From whom, and who sets the price?** Your suppliers; for each input the 2–5 biggest producers in the world or
   your region. The assistant may suggest names from public industry sources — you approve each one.
3. **How does it travel?** Country of origin, sea / rail / road, ports of loading and arrival. The assistant adds
   rows for the routes and ports (storms, closures, strikes) and, for sea freight from Asia, the public Drewry
   World Container Index (prompts/32_supply_chain.md tells it how to read it).
4. **Reference prices and currencies.** Futures and currency pairs as on finance.yahoo.com (e.g. `ALI=F` aluminium,
   `HG=F` copper, `TTF=F` EU gas, `EURUSD=X`, `EURCNY=X`). They are a *reference*, never your purchase price.
5. **Rules.** Duties or restrictions on your inputs (e.g. EU anti-dumping, chemical restrictions) — a news query each.
6. **Fill the watch list.** Old radar? `python3 scripts/radar_create.py --add-watch`. The assistant fills the sheet
   `Watchlist` in `data/floktron_radar.xlsx` with you: one row per item, `Active = Yes` only for what you approved.
   Thresholds: empty = `config.yaml → supply_chain` (5 % attention, 10 % urgent for a 5-day move); prices of
   commodities usually get 10 / 20, currencies 3 / 5.
7. **Test without writing:** `python3 scripts/supply_watch.py --dry`, then the weekly run `--full --dry`.
   Sources that do not answer are shown — the assistant records them in `Gaps`.
8. **First real run** writes the base line to `Watch_log` — the first week is your "normal".
9. **Switch on:** add to `config.yaml → schedule`: `supply: "19:10"` (every day) and `supply_week: "Mon 19:20"`,
   then run the installer again (`docs/INSTALL.md`). The AI part (reading candidates) runs with your evening
   news slice — `prompts/30_news_evening.md` step 6.
10. **After 4 weeks** look at the log together with the assistant and tune the thresholds: too many 🟡 → raise them.

## Limits — said plainly
- Public data only: no paid price services, no exchange feeds in real time; prices are end-of-day.
- A news title is not a fact. Every 🔴 candidate is read by the assistant before it reaches you, with the light check
  of `prompts/31_news_check.md`.
- Yahoo Finance, Google News or a supplier site may stop answering or change format — then you see ⚪ and a line in
  `Gaps`; nothing else breaks.
- FLOKTRON gives no forecasts and no investment advice. It shows what moved and where to look.


===== FILE: docs/WEBSITE.md =====

# Website — your own site, safe by default (Cloudflare recommended, any hosting works)

Optional. Do this **before the Marketing ray**: posts, social profiles, QR codes and e-mail signatures need one
address to point to. Your AI assistant leads you step by step; **you** click in the dashboards, type passwords
and approve every DNS change. The assistant never asks for passwords, tokens or API keys in the chat.

**Live example:** [koagu.com](https://koagu.com) runs on exactly this setup since 15.11.2026 — plain HTML/CSS/JS,
code in a private GitHub repository, hosting on Cloudflare Pages, six languages, forms, no cookie banner.
Steps 3–5 and 7–10 are what runs there, written so anyone can repeat it; step 6 is the recommended baseline on top.

## Why Cloudflare
| What | You get | You do not have to |
|---|---|---|
| **Certificates (HTTPS)** | issued and renewed automatically for your domain and `www` | buy, install or renew a certificate |
| **Protection** | DDoS protection and a global network in front of the site | run or patch a server |
| **Hosting** | static pages served from Cloudflare Pages; every push to GitHub goes live in about a minute | upload files by FTP |
| **Undo** | every change is a git commit; one click (or one revert) brings back the previous version | keep backups by hand |
| **More sites** | one account holds many sites — your shop on a subdomain, a partner's landing page, a product page | buy hosting for each |
| **Price** | the free plan is enough for a small business site with forms | — check current limits on cloudflare.com/plans |

## First question: where is your domain, and do you already have hosting?
Cloudflare is our recommendation, not a condition. The site files are plain HTML/CSS/JS and run on any hosting.
The assistant asks this first and follows one of four paths:

| Path | When | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **A. All on Cloudflare** (recommended) | new site, or you are free to choose | domain stays at your registrar, its nameservers point to Cloudflare, the site runs on Cloudflare Pages — steps 0–12 below as written |
| **B. Keep DNS at your registrar** | you cannot or do not want to move nameservers (Namecheap, GoDaddy, Hostinger, IONOS, a local registrar…) | site on Cloudflare Pages, `www` points there with a `CNAME`; the bare domain forwards to `www` at the registrar — see *Path B* below |
| **C. Your favourite hosting** | you already pay for hosting or like your provider (Namecheap, GoDaddy, Hostinger, IONOS, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages…) | same files, same checks; only the upload, HTTPS switch, headers and forms change — see *Path C* below |
| **D. Cloudflare in front of your hosting** | site stays where it is, you want the free protection on top | nameservers to Cloudflare (step 2), your site's `A`/`CNAME` record stays and is *proxied* (orange cloud), SSL mode *Full (strict)* |

Step 0 (keep your mail records), step 3 (the files), step 8 (never break a printed link), steps 10–12 (analytics,
legal pages, final check) are the same on every path.

## What you need
| Thing | Notes |
|---|---|
| A domain | from any registrar (where you bought it). You need its login — to change nameservers or DNS records |
| A Cloudflare account | sign up with a **company mailbox**, not a personal one; turn on 2-factor login at once |
| A GitHub account / organization | free; 2-factor login on; the site repository can be private |
| Time | about 1–2 hours of your clicks (estimate), plus waiting for the nameserver change (minutes to a day) |

## Who does what
| Your AI assistant | You |
|---|---|
| writes the site files, `_headers`, `_redirects`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, checks them | create the accounts, log in, click *Save* |
| lists the DNS records you have today and compares them after the move | change the nameservers at your registrar |
| tells you which button to press and what you should see | type every password and secret — only into Cloudflare / GitHub |
| checks the live site at the end (step 12) | decide what goes public |

## Step 0 — before you touch anything: list your DNS records
Your domain probably already carries **e-mail**. Losing these records means losing mail.
1. At your current DNS host (usually the registrar) open the DNS zone and **export it or take screenshots**.
2. Mark the records that must survive unchanged: `MX`, `TXT` with `v=spf1`, DKIM (`…._domainkey`), `_dmarc`,
   and every verification `TXT` (Google, Microsoft, your mail provider).
3. Rule for the whole setup: **mail and verification records are never changed or deleted** without the owner's
   explicit OK. The site only adds records for the site.

## Step 1 — accounts
1. Cloudflare: sign up → 2-factor login (app, not SMS) → save recovery codes offline.
2. GitHub: create an organization for the company (keeps the site separate from personal accounts) → 2-factor login.
3. Create a **private** repository, e.g. `company-site`.

## Step 2 — put the domain on Cloudflare
1. Cloudflare dashboard → *Add a domain* → type `example.com` → choose the **Free** plan.
2. Cloudflare imports the DNS records it finds. **Compare with your list from step 0** — add anything missing
   (mail records most of all). Mail records stay *DNS only* (grey cloud).
3. Cloudflare shows two nameservers. At your registrar replace the old nameservers with these two.
4. Wait until the domain shows **Active** (e-mail from Cloudflare). Then send a test e-mail to and from your domain.

*Cannot move nameservers? Use Path B or C above.*

## Step 3 — the site files
No builder, no framework: plain files that open in any browser. The assistant creates this layout:

```
company-site/
├── index.html            # or one folder per language: en/ lv/ ru/ …
├── assets/css/ assets/js/ assets/img/   # images as WebP, file names in Latin letters
├── 404.html
├── robots.txt
├── sitemap.xml
├── _headers              # security headers, cache, noindex for the test address
├── _redirects            # old addresses and printed QR codes → new pages
└── functions/            # only if you have forms (step 8)
```

Add a `README.md` that says what lives where — the next person (or AI assistant) will thank you.

## Step 4 — connect GitHub to Cloudflare Pages
1. Cloudflare → *Workers & Pages* → *Create* → **Pages** → *Connect to Git* → allow access **only to this one repository**.
2. Settings: production branch `main` · Framework preset **None** · Build command **empty** · Build output directory `/`.
3. *Save and Deploy*. The site appears at `company-site.pages.dev` — this is the **test address**.

*Cloudflare is moving Pages and Workers closer together; button names may differ slightly. The settings stay the same.*

## Step 5 — your own domain and certificates
1. Pages project → *Custom domains* → add `example.com`, then add `www.example.com`.
2. Cloudflare creates the records itself and issues the certificates. Wait until both show **Active** — usually minutes.
3. Choose **one main address** (koagu.com uses the bare domain `https://koagu.com`) and use it everywhere:
   canonical tags, sitemap, social profiles.

## Step 6 — HTTPS and security settings (domain → SSL/TLS, Security)
Recommended baseline — open each setting and check it once.

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SSL/TLS encryption mode | **Full (strict)** | never fall back to unencrypted traffic |
| Always Use HTTPS | **On** | `http://` becomes `https://` |
| Automatic HTTPS Rewrites | On | fixes old `http://` links inside pages |
| Minimum TLS version | **1.2** | drops outdated clients |
| DNSSEC | **On** → copy the DS record to your registrar | protects against forged DNS answers |
| Bot Fight Mode | optional | blocks simple bots; test your forms after switching it on |

## Step 7 — `_headers`: security and cache (copy, change the project name)
```
# Test addresses *.pages.dev are hidden from search engines
https://company-site.pages.dev/*
  X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow
https://:version.company-site.pages.dev/*
  X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow

/*
  X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
  X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
  Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
  Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()
  Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

/assets/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800
```
Changing CSS or JS? Add a version to the link (`site.css?v=2`) and raise it each time — visitors get the new file at once.

## Step 8 — `_redirects`: never break a printed link
```
/              /en/        302
/old-page      /en/new/    301
```
- Every address that was ever printed (QR codes on packages, flyers, business cards) gets a line and **is never removed**.
- **Lesson from koagu.com:** the old site sent `example.com → www`, the new one wanted `www → example.com`.
  Browsers remember a 301 for a long time, so old visitors got a redirect loop. Fix: keep the `www` rule **switched
  off** for a few months, let both addresses show the same site, and let the canonical tag point to the main one.
  Switch the rule on only later.

## Step 9 — forms without a server (optional)
Use Cloudflare **Pages Functions** (`functions/api/<name>.js`) and a **D1** database. Settings koagu.com uses:
| Point | How |
|---|---|
| Where data lives | D1 database created with **EU jurisdiction** |
| Spam | hidden honeypot field + minimum time to fill the form + limit of a few requests per hour per visitor |
| Visitor IP | only a **hash** is stored, never the IP itself |
| Retention | records older than 2 years are deleted automatically (state the same in your privacy policy) |
| Reading the requests | a private page behind password login, with CSV export for Excel |
| Login and passwords | Cloudflare → Pages project → *Settings* → *Variables and secrets*, type **Secret**. Never in code, never in the repository |
Your AI assistant writes the function; you create the database, bind it to the project (name `DB`) and enter the secrets.

## Step 10 — analytics and search engines
1. **Cloudflare Web Analytics** (Pages project → *Metrics*, or *Analytics & Logs* → *Web Analytics*): counts visits
   without cookies. With no other cookies on the site you need no cookie banner — check this against the rules of your country.
2. **Google Search Console** → *Domain* property → it gives a `TXT` record → add it in Cloudflare DNS → *Verify*
   → submit `https://example.com/sitemap.xml`. Bing Webmaster Tools can import from Search Console.
3. Each page: title, description, one H1, `canonical`, `hreflang` for every language version, a line in `sitemap.xml`.

## Step 11 — privacy and legal pages
- Privacy policy: what the forms collect, why, how long (step 9), processors (Cloudflare, your mail provider), where to complain.
- Terms of use; company details (name, registration number, address, e-mail) in the footer.
- German-speaking visitors: an *Impressum*; English: a *Legal notice*.
- Only true statements: no invented reviews, clients or logos.

## Step 12 — check before you announce (the assistant does it, you look)
| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| `https://example.com` | padlock, page opens |
| `http://example.com` | goes to `https://` |
| `https://www.example.com` | same site (or a redirect to the main address) |
| `company-site.pages.dev` | opens, response header `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` |
| Response headers on the main address | the lines from step 7 are there |
| A printed QR / old address | lands on the right new page |
| Forms | a test request arrives; a 6th quick request is refused |
| **E-mail** | a test message to and from your domain still arrives |
| `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, a wrong address | open; the wrong address shows your 404 page |

## Path B — DNS stays at your registrar, site on Cloudflare Pages
1. Do steps 1, 3 and 4 (accounts, files, Pages). Skip step 2.
2. Pages project → *Custom domains* → add `www.example.com`. Cloudflare shows a target like `company-site.pages.dev`.
3. At your registrar (DNS / Advanced DNS) add: `CNAME` · host `www` · value `company-site.pages.dev`. Do not touch mail records.
4. Bare domain `example.com`: Cloudflare Pages can serve it only when the domain is on Cloudflare nameservers.
   At the registrar use **URL forwarding / redirect** `example.com → https://www.example.com` (301). If your registrar
   offers `ALIAS`/`ANAME`/`CNAME flattening`, ask the assistant whether it fits.
5. The certificate for `www` is still issued and renewed by Cloudflare. Your main address is `https://www.example.com`.
6. Step 6 (HTTPS rules, DNSSEC) is done at the registrar instead — most offer *DNSSEC* and *HTTPS forwarding* switches.

## Path C — your favourite hosting
The same files work anywhere. What changes:

| Step | On Cloudflare Pages | On classic hosting (cPanel / hPanel / Plesk) | On Netlify / Vercel / GitHub Pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upload | push to GitHub | *Git Version Control* in the panel, or File Manager / SFTP into `public_html` | connect the GitHub repository |
| HTTPS | automatic | switch on the free certificate (*AutoSSL*, *Let's Encrypt*, *SSL/TLS*) and *Force HTTPS* | automatic; tick *Enforce HTTPS* |
| Headers (step 7) | `_headers` | `.htaccess` — snippet below | Netlify: `_headers` works as is; Vercel: `vercel.json` → `headers`; GitHub Pages: headers cannot be set |
| Redirects (step 8) | `_redirects` | `.htaccess` — `Redirect 301 /old-page /en/new/` | Netlify: `_redirects` works as is; Vercel: `vercel.json` → `redirects` |
| Forms (step 9) | Pages Functions + D1 | the host's PHP mail form or a form service — choose one that stores data in the EU, and name it in the privacy policy | Netlify Forms / Vercel functions |
| Analytics (step 10) | Web Analytics | Cloudflare Web Analytics works on any host: add its one-line script to every page (no cookies) | same |
| Test address hidden | `_headers` noindex | usually no test address; if the panel gives one, protect it with a password | Netlify / Vercel previews: add `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` for preview domains |

`.htaccess` for Apache hosting (most cPanel plans) — the assistant fills in your redirects:
```
RewriteEngine On
RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [L,R=301]

<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
  Header always set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"
  Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
  Header always set Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()"
  Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
</IfModule>

Redirect 301 /old-page /en/new/
ErrorDocument 404 /404.html
```
Hosting on nginx (no `.htaccess`)? Ask the provider's support to add the same headers and redirects — send them this list.
Later you can still move to Path A or add Path D: the files do not change.

## Day-to-day
- **Change** = edit a file → commit → push → live in about a minute (Path C classic hosting: upload, or pull in the panel).
- **Undo** = revert the commit, or Pages → *Deployments* → older version → *Rollback*.
- **Try first** = push to another branch → Cloudflare gives it its own preview address (hidden from search by step 7).
- **More sites** = one Pages project and one repository per site. Partners get their own project; give people access
  through Cloudflare *Members* with the smallest role needed — never share your own login.

## What FLOKTRON does here — and never does
- The assistant writes and checks files and tells you what to click. **No API token is needed** for this setup.
- It never logs in for you, never stores Cloudflare or GitHub passwords, never changes mail records.
- Want automation later (e.g. a script that publishes a page)? Create a Cloudflare API token limited to that one
  project and keep it in the system keychain — same rule as every FLOKTRON secret ([SECURITY_CHECKUP](SECURITY_CHECKUP.md)).

## If something does not work
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Mail stopped after the move | `MX`/SPF/DKIM record not imported | add it from your step 0 list, *DNS only* |
| "Too many redirects" | two opposite redirects (`www ↔ bare`), or SSL mode *Flexible* | keep one direction only; SSL mode *Full (strict)* |
| Custom domain stuck on *Pending* | nameservers not changed yet, or an old `A`/`CNAME` for the same name | wait for *Active*; delete the old record for that name |
| Old CSS after a change | browser cache | raise `?v=N` on every page |
| Form answers "error" | database not bound as `DB`, or secrets missing | Pages → *Settings* → *Bindings* / *Variables and secrets* |
| Test address shows up in Google | `_headers` noindex block missing | add it (step 7) |

## Next: the Marketing ray
Now posts, profiles and QR codes have one address. Link posts to the site with UTM labels
(`?utm_source=linkedin&utm_campaign=…`) and see the visits in Web Analytics. Set up the content plan next (setup wizard step 9).


===== FILE: docs/INVOICES.md =====

# Invoices → accounting — every supplier document read, checked against the bank, handed over

Supplier documents come in every language and shape: a Latvian *rēķins*, a German *Rechnung*, a Spanish *factura
proforma*, an Estonian *ettemaksuarve*, a scan from a phone, the same invoice forwarded twice, a delivery note that is
not an invoice at all. FLOKTRON reads them, checks each one against your bank statement and gives the finance ray
(by default L7) short tasks: what to pay, what to check, which final invoice to ask for, what to pass to the accountant.

**Tested before release on a fictional set** (no real company inside, every page marked *TEST · FICTIONAL*):
10 documents in 7 languages (LV, EN, DE, ES, LT, ET, RU) plus a Czech scan without a text layer, and a bank statement
as PDF and as CSV — `tests/fixtures/invoices/`. Try it yourself in one line (dry run, writes nothing):

```
python3 scripts/invoices.py --folder tests/fixtures/invoices/docs --extraction tests/fixtures/invoices/extraction.json \
  --statements tests/fixtures/invoices/statements_csv --today 2026-11-22 --test
```

## Two steps

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Read | your AI assistant (`prompts/50_invoices.md`) | opens every new document (PDF, photo, scan), writes one record per document into `data/invoices/extraction.json`: supplier, VAT number, type, number, dates, net / VAT / total, how it is paid, words that identify the supplier in a bank payment. Never invents a figure: what it cannot read stays empty and is flagged |
| 2. Check and hand over | `scripts/invoices.py` (no AI, no network) | skips duplicates, finds every payment in your bank statement, sets a status, writes the sheet **Invoices** and tasks for the finance ray; the dashboard shows the card *Invoices → accounting* |

## What it catches

| Situation | Status | Task |
|---|---|---|
| Paid, payment found (invoice number or supplier name + amount + date) | `Paid <date>` | — (goes into the hand-over task) |
| The same document forwarded again (`FW_ …`, `(1).pdf`), a scan and a photo of the same invoice, or already in the base (number compared without spaces, dashes and case: `PR-2026/118` = `pr 2026 118`) | not added | — |
| A record with an empty total, number or date, or an unknown type (the assistant could not read it) | not booked, listed as *needs a look* until the record is corrected | — (tell the person) |
| Delivery note / *Lieferschein* / *pavadzīme* without amounts | `Not a payment document`, linked to its invoice | — |
| Proforma paid, final invoice set off against it | proforma `Closed by invoice …`, invoice `Paid by advance` | — |
| Proforma, order confirmation or advance invoice paid, no final invoice | `Paid · no final invoice` | ask the supplier for the final invoice |
| Not paid, due date ahead | `To pay by <date>` | pay by the due date |
| Not found in the statement | `Not found in statement` | check the payment |
| Same amount paid to someone else (e.g. a supermarket card payment) | **not** taken as the payment — `(similar payment)` | check the payment, with the similar one named |
| Same amount in another currency; a short number like `12` that also appears in a date; only a legal form (`SIA`, `GmbH`) in common | **not** taken as the payment | check the payment |
| VAT of another country charged / reverse charge | comment on the row | one task for the accountant (ESTIMATE — to confirm) |
| Several orders paid with one card payment | `one payment for N documents` | — |

## Folders (all inside your own `data/`, never in git)

```
data/invoices/inbox/<supplier>/<file>.pdf     ← documents, one folder per supplier (any names, any language)
data/invoices/statements/<file>.csv|.pdf      ← bank statements you download yourself
data/invoices/extraction.json                 ← what the assistant read (step 1)
```

**Bank statements.** Download them yourself from the internet bank — FLOKTRON never logs in to a bank.
CSV from any bank works (columns *date, counterparty, details, amount*, optional *currency*, in EN / LV / LT / ET / DE
names; incoming money is skipped — by the D/K column, or by the sign when outgoing payments are negative). The same
payment in two overlapping statements (October and October–November) counts once. PDF statements in the Swedbank layout work too if `pip install pypdf` is done; otherwise the script says so
and asks for CSV. Only statements of **your** account are read (`invoices.our_iban` in `config.yaml`); a private account
statement in the same folder is skipped.

## config.yaml

```yaml
invoices:
  our_iban: "LV00BANK0000000000000"   # your company account in the statements
  our_vat: "LV00000000000"            # your VAT number; its country is "home" for the VAT check
  ray: L7                             # who gets the tasks (finance)
```

## Rules

- **Nothing is paid, sent or deleted.** Tasks go into the morning message of the finance ray like any other task.
- **Dry run first**: `python3 scripts/invoices.py` shows everything and writes nothing; `--apply` writes.
- **Raw materials stay codes.** The base keeps supplier, number, dates and amounts — no product names, recipes or quantities.
- Every VAT remark is an ESTIMATE for your accountant to confirm, never advice.
- Supplier names and numbers come from outside: they are written as plain text, never as spreadsheet formulas.
- Test with fictional data first (`--test`: rows and tasks are marked TEST, the dashboard shows them with a *test* tag).


===== FILE: docs/SNAPSHOT.md =====

# Company snapshot — the state of your company on one date, in one file

A partner asks "where are you now?", an investor wants a one-pager before a call, the tax office asks for a summary.
Each time someone gathers the same facts again by hand. FLOKTRON builds them in one command:

- a **PDF** to read — branded with your colours, in English, Latvian or Russian;
- a **JSON** file for machines — the same rows, each with its **status** and **source**, plus the SHA-256 of the PDF,
  so anyone can check that the two files belong to one snapshot.

**You decide what goes out.** Pick a profile, then add or remove whole sections. What is marked *secret* never leaves.

Try it on the fictional company first (writes into `/tmp/snapshot`, touches nothing of yours):

```
python3 scripts/snapshot.py --test --all --out /tmp/snapshot
```

## Profiles

| Profile | For whom | What is in it |
|---|---|---|
| `partner` | a partner or investor, **after an NDA** | company, people, product and IP, stock / orders / purchases, invoices, finance, contracts, bank. Valuation only with `--plus valuation` |
| `no_bank` | the same, when bank details should stay home | as `partner`, without bank account and balances |
| `tax` | the tax office | company, people, operations, invoices, finance, contracts, bank — **only PUBLIC and DEAL figures**: no estimates, no plans |
| `public` | anyone | company, people, product — only PUBLIC facts marked `public` |

Add or remove sections: `--plus valuation`, `--minus bank,contracts`.
Sections: `company, people, product_ip, operations, invoices, finance, contracts, bank, valuation`.

## Every figure has a status

| Status | Means |
|---|---|
| PUBLIC | from an open source — a register, an annual report, your website |
| DEAL | a signed document or a completed transaction — a contract, an invoice, a bank statement |
| ESTIMATE | your own calculation |
| SCENARIO | a plan, not a fact |

A fact with an unknown status is treated as ESTIMATE — never shown as a fact.

## Your facts — `data/snapshot/facts.json`

Your AI assistant fills it with you (`prompts/51_snapshot.md`): public facts from the business register, the rest only
from you or your own files. One record per fact:

```json
{"company": {"name": "Example SIA", "reg_no": "40000000000", "vat_no": "LV40000000000", "address": "…"},
 "facts": [
  {"section": "finance", "id": "turnover_2025", "label": {"en": "Turnover 2025", "lv": "Apgrozījums 2025. g."},
   "value": "18 400,00 EUR", "status": "PUBLIC", "source": "annual report 2025", "as_of": "2026-05-31",
   "sensitivity": "public"}
 ]}
```

`sensitivity` decides who may see it:

| sensitivity | Goes into |
|---|---|
| `public` | every profile |
| `nda` | `partner`, `no_bank`, `tax` |
| `bank` | `partner`, `tax` (never `no_bank`, never `public`) |
| `valuation` | only when you add `--plus valuation` |
| `internal` | nowhere — notes for yourself |
| `secret` | **nowhere, ever** — and an unknown value counts as secret |

From the base (`data/floktron_base.xlsx`) the snapshot adds **counts and totals only**: stock lines, orders by status,
open purchases, rental items out, supplier invoices and what is still open. Names of clients and sites are never read.

## The lock

Not a switch. Before anything is written, the whole snapshot is checked for locked words — built in: passwords, keys,
tokens, PIN codes, recipes, formulations. Add your own in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
snapshot:
  facts: data/snapshot/facts.json
  out: data/snapshot/out
  locked_words: ["our secret ingredient", "prototype X"]
```

One hit stops the run, says which word was found, and **nothing is written**.

## For the tax office

The snapshot is **not a tax return**. Tax e-services take returns only in their own forms. The PDF can be attached to a
free-form application — in Latvia, an *Iesniegums* in the VID EDS. XML drafts of specific tax forms may come later; a
return is always checked and filed by you or your accountant.

## Rules

- Nothing is sent. You decide where each file goes.
- Read only: the facts file and the base are never changed.
- Make one snapshot per recipient and date; the JSON keeps only the number of rows left out, not what they were.
- PDF needs `pip install reportlab`; without it the JSON is written and the script says so.


===== FILE: docs/DOCUMENTS.md =====

# Documents — invoices, advance invoices, acts and offers in your own brand

Most small companies write invoices in an online form or a word processor: a different look every time, numbers
kept by hand, nothing in the books until someone types it in. FLOKTRON makes the four documents a small company
sends most often, on one branded sheet, with the number and the register row done for you:

| Type | LV name | What is on it |
|---|---|---|
| `invoice` | Rēķins | all fields of an EU VAT invoice: seller and buyer with reg. and VAT numbers, number, date, delivery date, lines, net / VAT / total, amount in words, bank details, due date, "valid without signature" |
| `advance` | Avansa rēķins | the same, for a prepayment; says that a final invoice follows delivery |
| `act` | Pieņemšanas-nodošanas akts | goods or services handed over and accepted, two signature fields |
| `offer` | Komercpiedāvājums | lines and prices, valid-until date, notes, who offers |

Languages: `lv`, `en` or `lv+en` (both on one sheet, for buyers abroad). Colours come from the `colors` section of
`config.yaml` (the same as your messages), plus your logo.

**Tested before release on fictional data** (Demo SIA and its buyers do not exist; every page carries
*TEST · FICTIONAL*). Try it in one line — writes one PDF, touches nothing else:

```
python3 scripts/documents.py --seller tests/fixtures/documents/seller_demo.json \
  --doc tests/fixtures/documents/invoice_lv.json --out data/documents/test
```

## How it works

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Ask | you, in words: *"invoice to Paraugs Būve, 4 chairs, due in 10 days"* | |
| 2. Fill | your AI assistant (`prompts/52_documents.md`) | writes `data/documents/in/<date>_<type>_<buyer>.json`: buyer from your own records or the public business register, lines and prices **only from your price list or from you**. Never invents a price, a VAT number or a bank account |
| 3. Make | `scripts/documents.py` (no AI, no network) | draws the PDF, takes the next number, adds the amount in words. Dry run first: nothing is recorded |
| 4. Record | you say *"yes"* → the same line with `--apply` | the number is fixed and one row goes to the sheet **Issued** in your base |
| 5. Send | **you** | FLOKTRON never sends a document to a customer by itself |

Payments: the invoices you issued can be checked against the bank statement the same way as supplier invoices
([INVOICES](INVOICES.md)).

## Setting up — the `documents` section of `config.yaml`

```yaml
documents:                 # optional: branded invoices, acts, offers (docs/DOCUMENTS.md)
  legal_name: ""           # as in the register, e.g. SIA "Example"; empty = company.name
  reg_no: ""
  vat_no: ""               # empty if you are not VAT registered (then use "vat_rate": 0 and say why in "notes")
  address: ""
  email: ""                # the public company address
  phone: ""
  web: ""
  bank: ""
  swift: ""
  iban: ""
  prefix: "INV"            # numbers look like INV-R-2026-001 (R invoice, AR advance, A act, P offer)
  logo: ""                 # PNG with a transparent background, next to config.yaml or a full path
```

Needs `reportlab` (`pip install reportlab`) and a font with Latvian letters — Liberation Sans, Arial or DejaVu Sans
(on macOS Arial is already there).

## The document file

```json
{"type": "invoice", "lang": "lv", "date": "2026-11-23", "due_days": 10, "supply_date": "2026-11-23",
 "buyer": {"name": "SIA \"Buyer\"", "reg_no": "…", "vat_no": "…", "address": "…", "email": "…"},
 "basis": "Contract No. 1",
 "lines": [{"desc": "Product", "note": "small grey line under it", "qty": 4, "unit": "pcs", "price": 89.90}],
 "vat_rate": 21, "notes": "optional"}
```

`act` may add `"place"`; `offer` adds `"valid_until"`, `"intro"`, `"signed_by"`; `"show_prices": false` hides prices
on an act; `"number"` fixes a number by hand (it is refused if it is already in the register); `"test": true`
prints the *TEST · FICTIONAL* mark.

## Rules that keep it safe

- **Numbers are never reused.** A wrong document gets a new number and a note in the base — the old row stays.
- **Dry run first**; `--apply` only after the person has seen the PDF.
- **No invented figures.** Prices, VAT numbers and bank accounts come from the person, the price list or a public
  register — never from memory.
- **EU buyers with a VAT number:** `"vat_rate": 0` and a note (e.g. *Intra-Community supply of goods, Directive
  2006/112/EC Art. 138*) — check the buyer's number in VIES first; when in doubt, ask your accountant.
- Your data stays on your computer: documents are in `data/documents/`, never in git.


===== FILE: docs/FOLLOWUPS.md =====

# Follow-ups — polite reminders after an offer, only after your OK

An offer goes out, the buyer is busy, and a week later nobody remembers to ask. FLOKTRON keeps count for you:
on day 3, 7 and 14 after an offer was sent it writes a short, polite reminder in the language of the offer and asks
**you** first. Nothing reaches a buyer until you press ✅.

**Tested before release on fictional data** (Demo SIA and its buyers do not exist; addresses are `@example.com`;
nothing is sent — outgoing mail is written as files). Try it: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_followups.py`.

## How it works

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Offer | you, with `scripts/documents.py` ([DOCUMENTS](DOCUMENTS.md)) | the offer gets a number (`<prefix>-P-<year>-NNN`) and a row in the sheet **Issued** with the language and the buyer's e-mail |
| 2. Sent | **you** send it from your mailbox | `scripts/followups.py` finds the message by the offer number in the subject or in the PDF name — that day is day 0 |
| 3. Watch | `scripts/followups.py` (no AI), with the other automatic runs | looks for any answer: from the same address, or from a colleague at the same company domain (free mail domains such as gmail.com do not count). Auto-replies and mailing lists do not count |
| 4. Ask you | day 3, 7, 14 — Monday to Friday, working hours | a message to the manager with the draft and three buttons: **✅ Send**, **✏️ My text**, **⏸ No more reminders** |
| 5. Send | after ✅ or ✏️ | the reminder goes as a **reply in the same thread**, only to the address the offer went to, only in working hours |
| 6. Stop | automatically | the buyer answered, the offer status became Accepted / Declined / Closed / Paid / Cancelled, or you pressed ⏸ |

A draft you did not answer before the next one is due becomes *Outdated*; the next one replaces it. Two reminders
never go out less than three days apart. Everything is in the sheet **Follow-ups** of your base — one row per step,
and the column *Decision* can be filled by hand (`OK` or `NO`).

## The three reminders (built in, LV and EN)

| Day | Idea |
|---|---|
| 3 | Did the offer arrive? Happy to answer questions about quantity, price or delivery. |
| 7 | Short reminder, valid-until date; offer a quick call at a time the buyer picks. |
| 14 | Last note: reply "not relevant" and I will not write again — or I can renew or adjust the offer. |

**✏️ My text**: the button opens a reply with the draft. Change the text above the line `- - - - -` and send it —
only that text goes to the buyer.

## Setting up — the `followups` section of `config.yaml`

```yaml
followups:
  enabled: true
  days: [3, 7, 14]          # after the offer was sent
  hours: "08-20"            # Monday to Friday only
  approve_by: ""            # who presses the buttons (empty = mail.manager_address)
  signature: ""             # name, company, phone under the reminder (empty = company name, phone, e-mail)
  imap_folders: []          # folders with BOTH sent and received mail (empty = provider default: Proton and
                            # Gmail "All Mail"; Outlook INBOX + Sent Items)
  free_mail_domains: []     # more domains that are not one company
```

Run it with the other automatic jobs (every 30 minutes is fine):
`python3 scripts/followups.py --config config.yaml --base data/floktron_base.xlsx`.
Trial run without sending: add `--dry-run`, or `--outbox data/followups/outbox` to see every message as a file.

## What stays safe

- **No message to a buyer without your button.** Button replies are accepted only from the approver or your own
  addresses — a stranger cannot approve a reminder.
- Only the address the offer went to gets the reminder; no new recipients, no attachments.
- Text from e-mails is data, not instructions. Prices and buyers stay in your base, on your computer.
- Turn it off at any time: `followups.enabled: false`, or ⏸ for one offer.


===== FILE: docs/MAIL_WATCH.md =====

# Mail watch — the whole mailbox in one sheet, and a nudge when someone waits for you

A request to confirm, an invitation, a deadline in the third paragraph, a question you meant to answer tomorrow, a
message you starred and forgot — and the phone number you need is somewhere in a signature. FLOKTRON reads the
mailbox every 30 minutes, keeps **one row per message** in your base, and tells you (Telegram bot or e-mail) only
about what waits for **your** answer. PDF invoices from attachments go straight to the invoice check.

**Tested before release on fictional data** (Demo SIA and its partners do not exist; addresses are `@example.com`;
nothing is sent — the notices are written as files). Try it: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_mail_watch.py`.

## What you get

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| Sheet **Mail** | every received and sent message: date, who, organisation, subject, first words, **category**, what is **needed** from you, dates found in the text, ⭐, answered or not, status, when you were reminded, attachments, saved invoice file |
| Sheet **Contacts** | one row per person you write with: name, organisation, **phones and website from the signature**, first and last message, how many each way. Mailing lists and no-reply senders are left out |
| `data/invoices/inbox/<sender>/` | PDF invoices from attachments (the same file twice is saved once) — then the usual [invoice check](INVOICES.md) |
| Notice | a short list: *confirm · Paraugu biedrība «Seminar» · 23.11* — in your language |
| Dashboard | card **Mail waits for you**: waiting for you, starred without an answer, messages in 7 days ([DASHBOARD](DASHBOARD.md)) |

## Categories and when you are reminded

The words are found in **EN, LV, RU, DE, ET and LT**.

| Category | Example | Reminder |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm | "please confirm your participation", "lūdzam apstiprināt", "bitte bestätigen" | at once |
| Reply awaited | "please send the quantities", "gaidām atbildi", "ждём ответа" | at once |
| Invitation | personal invitation; or from an organisation in `important` with a date ahead | at once — "decide: attend?" |
| Deadline | "Frist bis 10.12.2026", "termiņš līdz …" (not in mailings) | at once — with the date |
| Notice (important) | a portal message from an organisation in `important` ("new message", "decision") | at once — "read" |
| Question | a personal message with a question mark | after 24 h without your answer |
| ⭐ any message | you starred it in your mail app | after 48 h without your answer |
| Invoice | PDF named or sent as an invoice | no reminder: saved → invoice check |
| Service confirmation | a service asks you to "verify your e-mail", "confirm your account", "apstipriniet e-pastu" | **never** — clicking the link ends it; it is not a task |
| Letter · Newsletter · Notice · Auto-reply · Code / login · FLOKTRON (system) · Sent | "we received your submission" is a Notice too | never |

- Then again on **day 3, 7 and 14** after the message came (`mail_watch.remind_days`), then never — no fanaticism;
  nothing in quiet hours (22–07) — it waits for the morning.
- **You answered** — the reminder stops by itself: a sent message that replies to it, the flag *Answered*, or **any later
  message from you to that address or that company's domain** (a call and then a new letter count — the correspondence goes on).
- No answer after day 14 (`mail_watch.close_after_days`) → status `Closed · 14 days`.
- In **Telegram** every letter is its own message with two buttons **✅ Answered · ⛔ Not needed** (at most 5 per run);
  a press closes it — no sheets, no columns ([Telegram](TELEGRAM.md#tasks-yes--no)). `Closed` in the column **Status** works too.
- Messages older than 48 h from before the first run are only written to the sheet — no flood on day one.

## Invoices from mail → accounting, by themselves

1. FLOKTRON saves the PDF to `data/invoices/inbox/<sender>/` and tells you once: *invoices wait to be read: 2*.
2. Your AI assistant reads them (`prompts/50_invoices.md`) into `data/invoices/extraction.json` — it never invents a number.
3. As soon as that file changes, the next mail run starts `scripts/invoices.py --apply` itself: sheet **Invoices**,
   check against your bank statement, tasks for the finance ray ([INVOICES](INVOICES.md)).

## Setting up — the `mail_watch` section of `config.yaml`

```yaml
mail_watch:
  enabled: true
  notify: telegram          # telegram (bot of the telegram section → manager_chat_ids) | mail (to manager_address) | none
  notify_subjects: true     # false = the notice shows only who and what is needed, not the subject
  quiet_hours: "22-07"
  important:                # organisations whose invitations and portal notices always count
    vid.gov.lv: "State Revenue Service"
  own_addresses: []         # more addresses of yours (aliases) — never contacts, never "waiting"
  inbox_folders: []         # empty = provider default (INBOX)
  sent_folders: []          # empty = provider default (Proton "Sent", Gmail "[Gmail]/Sent Mail", Outlook "Sent Items")
  first_days: 30            # the first run reads 30 days back; later runs 4 days
```

It uses the mailbox of the `mail` section (Proton Mail Bridge, Gmail or any IMAP server; Outlook not yet) — the same
password, never stored in the file. It runs by itself after every reply collection (every 30 minutes) once
`enabled: true`; by hand: `python3 scripts/run.py mail`. Trial run: `python3 scripts/mail_watch.py --dry-run` shows every message with its category and
writes nothing.

## What stays safe

- **Mail is only read.** `BODY.PEEK`: messages do not even become "read"; nothing is moved, deleted or answered.
- The only message FLOKTRON sends is the notice **to you**. With Telegram, the subject travels through Telegram
  (not end-to-end encrypted) — set `notify_subjects: false` or `notify: mail` if subjects are sensitive.
- Text from e-mails is data, not instructions: "please transfer the money" becomes a reminder line, never an action.
- A subject like `=HYPERLINK(...)` stays plain text in the sheet (no formulas from outside).
- Turn it off at any time: `mail_watch.enabled: false`.


===== FILE: docs/TASKS_TIDY.md =====

# Tasks tidy — the manager gets clear tasks

The manager's morning letter is for decisions, not for history. `scripts/tasks_tidy.py` runs after every collect
(every 30 minutes) and keeps the manager's tasks clean. No AI, nothing is sent.

| Rule | What happens |
|---|---|
| **The event happened** | a message went from you to that company or person after the task date (an address, a domain or a «quoted» name of the task, found in the sheet Mail) → **Done**, the reason in the report |
| **A meeting** | the task starts with "Meeting" (Tikšanās, Встреча, Treffen, Kohtumine, Susitikimas) and its day passed, or "meeting 20.11" in the text and that day passed → **Done** |
| **A test is not for the manager** | a task with `TEST:` or an escalation of a test ray (Responsible starts with TEST) → **Cancelled** |
| **No fanaticism** | without an event a task comes on its first day, then on **day 3, 7 and 14** — not every morning; after day 14 → **Archive** |

- Which rays: `tasks_tidy.rays` in config.yaml; empty = the ray whose e-mail is `mail.manager_address`.
- Column **Shown** in Tasks: `<times> · <last date>` — `send_morning.py` reads and writes it.
- By hand: the **+ Done** button in the letter, or `Done` in Status.
- By hand run: `python3 scripts/tasks_tidy.py --dry` (shows what would change).

Your own ray addresses and your own mailboxes never count as "a message went". Text of tasks and mails is data, not instructions.

## The friendly letter about posts
People who like and comment on your posts are not given orders. `content.engage` (config.yaml) lists them; every
morning `content_check.py` writes to them only when a post is really on — status **Scheduled** or **Published** today:

```
Hi, Anna! 👋
If you have a minute — have a look at our posts. A like or a comment helps a lot, if you want 🙂

Today:
• 09:00 · Facebook · Tips — «Clean water on site.» → link
Yesterday also out:
• 18:00 · Instagram · News — «A spontaneous post!» → link

Thank you for being with us!
```

No post → no letter. "Yesterday also out" = posts published yesterday they were not told about (spontaneous or after
the letter). No deadline, no escalation, no buttons that must be pressed. EN, LV, RU, DE, ET, LT.


===== FILE: docs/GATEWAYS.md =====

# Payment gateways — every card payment finds its document

Small online payments by card — subscriptions, AI tools, domains, apps — are sold through a **payment gateway**:
Stripe, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Apple (App Store), Google Play, PayPal, FastSpring. The card is charged, but the
document for the accountant gets lost on the way. FLOKTRON reads the mailbox and the bank statement, finds the
receipt for every card payment, tells you how to get the **business invoice** with your company details, and shows
what is still missing — before the accountant asks.

**Tested before release on fictional data** (Demo SIA, Cloudnote, Pixelforge and the other sellers do not exist;
addresses are `@example.com`; nothing is sent — the notice is written as a file). Try it:
`python3 -m pytest tests/test_gateways.py`.

## Where the document gets lost

| Place | What happens | What FLOKTRON does |
|---|---|---|
| Mailbox | the receipt has no PDF — only a link to the gateway's portal | a PDF copy of the message (marked "not an invoice") + a task "download the business invoice" |
| Mailbox | the PDF is called `Receipt-…` and no invoice filter catches it | it is saved to `data/invoices/inbox/<seller>/` → the usual [invoice check](INVOICES.md) |
| Mailbox | the receipt landed in **Spam** | the spam folder is read too (only read) |
| Mailbox | Apple / Google receipts live only in the message text | amount, seller and order number are read from the text |
| Bank statement | the invoice check looks for a payment for every document, not a document for every payment | every card payment looks for its document |
| Bank statement | payments in USD or GBP are skipped | the original amount, the rate and the conversion fee are read; the EUR amount is kept |
| Seller | a private-person receipt without your company name and VAT number | the exact place in the gateway's portal where you add them; a draft request to the seller's support |

## What you get

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| Sheet **Gateways** | one row per receipt and per card payment: gateway, seller, amount, currency, charged EUR, receipt number, document, file, **how to get the business invoice**, payment in the statement, status |
| `data/invoices/inbox/<seller>/` | `YYYY-MM-DD_<Seller>_<Amount><CUR>.pdf` — the receipt PDF, or a PDF copy of the message |
| `data/gateways/requests/` | a draft request in English to the seller's support for the business invoice — **never sent**; none for Apple / Google (their portal is the place) |
| `data/gateways/acts/` | a **draft** internal act (LV + EN) for a card payment with no document after `act_days` days — for the head of the company to sign. *Estimate: check with your accountant whether an act is accepted in your case.* |
| Tasks | for the finance ray: *download the business invoice*, *find the receipt*, *sign the internal acts* |
| Notice | one short message: *card payments without a document: 3 · business invoice needed: 2* — not in quiet hours |

## How a payment is matched

A card payment and a receipt belong together only when **all** of these agree: the same amount and currency,
the payment date within −3 … +7 days of the receipt, **and** the seller's name or the gateway is written in the
statement line. Amount and date alone are never enough — two 9.99 subscriptions in one week stay apart.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| PDF → invoice check | the receipt came as a PDF — it is saved for the usual invoice check (· *payment found* when the card line is there) |
| Business invoice needed from the portal | no PDF, or a private-person receipt — follow *How to get the business invoice* |
| Payment without a document — find the receipt | a card payment without any document — the column says where this gateway keeps it |
| No document for N days → draft internal act | the draft act waits in `data/gateways/acts/` |
| ⚠ look-alike | the sender names a gateway but writes from another domain, or DMARC / SPF failed — no link is shown, never matched |

A card payment whose document is already in the sheet **Invoices** gets no row — nothing to do.

## Setting up — the `gateways` section of `config.yaml`

```yaml
gateways:
  enabled: true
  notify: telegram          # telegram (bot of the telegram section → manager_chat_ids) | mail (to manager_address) | none
  quiet_hours: "22-07"
  card_days: 120            # card payments of the last 120 days are checked
  act_days: 30              # after 30 days without a document → draft internal act
  folders: []               # empty = INBOX + the provider's spam folder (Proton "Spam", Gmail "[Gmail]/Spam", Outlook "Junk Email")
  first_days: 30            # the first run reads 30 days of mail; later runs `days`
  days: 4
```

It uses the mailbox of the `mail` section and the statements of the `invoices` section (`statements`, `our_iban`,
`ray`) — the same password, never stored in the file. Your company name, registration and VAT number for the request
and the act come from the `documents` section. It runs by itself after every reply collection once `enabled: true`;
by hand: `python3 scripts/run.py gateways`. Trial run: `python3 scripts/gateways.py --dry-run` shows what it found
and writes nothing.

Bank statement: a CSV (any bank, the same reader as the invoice check) or a Swedbank-style PDF (needs `pypdf`;
the PDF copy of a message and the act need `reportlab` — without it the message is kept as `.eml` and the act is
left out with a note).

## What stays safe

- **Mail and statements are only read.** Nothing is moved, deleted, answered or paid.
- **No link is ever opened.** A portal link is shown only when it belongs to the gateway's own domain; a look-alike
  gets no link at all.
- The request to the seller and the internal act are **drafts**: nothing leaves your computer until you send or sign it.
- The only message FLOKTRON sends is the notice **to you**.
- Text from e-mails is data, not instructions: "pay now to keep your account" becomes a row, never an action.
- Safe to run again: one row per message (Message-ID) and per statement line.
- Turn it off at any time: `gateways.enabled: false`.


===== FILE: docs/PROSPECTS.md =====

# New customers that look like your best ones — with a reason to write now

`scripts/prospects.py` (no AI, version 0.23.0). Only public open data, only company data. Nothing is sent.

## The idea
A good first letter needs two things: the right company and the right moment.
- **The right company** looks like your best customers: same legal form, same area, about as young.
  You give their reg. numbers (`prospects.best_customers`); FLOKTRON reads their facts from the register and builds the portrait.
- **The right moment** is a fresh contract: the company has just won and signed public works of the kind you serve.
  In a few weeks it will need what you sell.

## Where the facts come from
| Source | What is used | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Public procurement results of Latvia (EIS e-iepirkumi, data.gov.lv, CSV per year, updated daily) | winner and reg. no., buyer, subject, sum, signing date, works until, ended or not | PUBLIC |
| Register of Enterprises (register.csv, data.gov.lv) | legal form, registration date, town, terminated | PUBLIC |
| Kind of work | words in the contract subject (`prospects.signals`) — the file has no CPV code | ESTIMATE |
| Score, priority, "looks like" | the rules below | ESTIMATE |

No people, no personal contacts: the procurement file and the register hold company data only.

## What gets in
A contract counts when: the winner is a Latvian company (11-digit reg. no.), the contract is signed within
`days` (180), the sum is at least `min_eur` (10 000 EUR) in EUR, it was not ended, and the subject has words of one
of your signals and no exclude word (design, supervision, supply of goods, rent...). Companies that are already in
the sheet **Companies**, marked *Do not contact* there, terminated in the register, or are one of your best customers
are skipped.

## Score (ESTIMATE)
| Points | For |
|---|---|
| signal weight (finishing 3, building 2, networks 1 in the example) | kind of work |
| 3 / 2 / 1 | signed within 30 / 90 / 180 days |
| +1 | the works are still under way |
| +2 / +1 | contract up to `small_max_eur` / up to 5 × that (the size of a small contractor) |
| −2 | wins over `big_total_eur` in 12 months (a big general contractor) |
| +1 | two or more wins in 12 months |
| +1 each | same legal form, same area, not older than your oldest best customer + 3 years |

Priority 1 from 9 points, 2 from 6, else 3. At most `max_new` (40) new rows per run.

## Sheet "Prospects" (radar base)
ID, Found, Company, Reg. no., Score, Priority, **Why now** (e.g. "signed 10.11.2026 · 84 500 EUR · remont; works under way"),
Contract subject, Buyer, Sum EUR, Signed, Works until, Wins 12 months, Form, Town, Registered, Looks like,
Source (link to the procurement), Data status, **Decision**, Status, Draft, Comment.

**Decision**
- `Add` → the company goes to the sheet **Companies** (goal Client, work status New) and a draft first letter is
  written to `data/prospects/drafts/<ID>_<company>.txt` from your template (`prospects.letter`, placeholders
  `{company}`, `{works}`, `{pitch}`, `{product_line}`, `{signature}`).
- `No` → never suggested again.

The draft is **not sent**. You find the company's GENERAL address on its own website, check the text and send it
yourself — one personal business letter to one company, with a line to opt out. That is the line between a
business letter and spam; FLOKTRON does not cross it.

## Notice
When a run finds new prospects: one short Telegram message or e-mail (like mail watch, `prospects.notify`) with
the number and the top 3. No new prospects — no message.

## Settings (`config.yaml`)
```yaml
prospects:
  enabled: false
  notify: telegram          # telegram | mail | none
  best_customers: []        # reg. numbers of your best customers, e.g. ["40000000001"]
  home_area: []             # town words; empty = the towns of your best customers
  days: 180
  min_eur: 10000
  pitch: ""                 # two sentences for the draft letter
  letter: ""                # your own template file (optional)
  signals: [...]            # see config.example.yaml; stems in the language of the file; first match wins, `unless` steps aside
```

## Run
```
python3 scripts/prospects.py --dry-run          # look first, write nothing
python3 scripts/run.py prospects                # the daily run (scheduler: once a day, e.g. 07:20)
python3 scripts/prospects.py --eis-csv results.csv --register-csv register.csv   # files you downloaded yourself
```
Network: only data.gov.lv, through `scripts/registry_lv.py` (see `docs/TRANSPARENCY.md`).
Tests: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_prospects.py` — fictional companies (TEST · FICTIONAL), files built at test time.

## Limits
- Only Latvia so far (the EIS and UR open data). Other countries: the same columns from your own CSV via `--eis-csv`.
- The kind of work comes from words, not from a CPV code — read the subject before you write.
- Public contracts only; private building sites are not in any open file.


===== FILE: docs/INDUSTRY_PACKS.md =====

# Industry packs — the radar ready on day one

The radar finds news, tenders and consultations by the company's own keywords. Writing 30 good keywords in three
languages takes an evening. An industry pack is a ready, neutral start: the company keeps what fits, removes the rest
and adds its own words. Nothing in a pack is secret and nothing is sent anywhere — it is a file in `templates/industry/`.

## Packs

| Pack | For | Keywords | Languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| `construction` | builders, finishing and renovation crews, building-material suppliers, construction services | 24 (10 every run, 14 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |
| `logistics` | road haulage, freight forwarding, warehousing, courier and last-mile companies | 24 (9 every run, 15 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |
| `wholesale` | wholesalers and distributors: food, building materials, equipment, consumables | 24 (9 every run, 15 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |
| `production` | manufacturers and workshops: metal, wood, food, plastics, building products, contract manufacturing | 24 (9 every run, 15 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |
| `rental` | rental of construction machinery, tools, scaffolding, generators, cabins and vehicles | 24 (8 every run, 16 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |
| `services` | companies serving other companies: cleaning, facility management, security, maintenance and repair | 24 (8 every run, 16 first run of the month) | LV, RU, EN |

A company in two industries can apply two packs — every pack has its own IDs, nothing is added twice. A pack for another industry: copy `construction.json`, change the words, keep the format.

## Three questions at setup

The setup wizard (step 7) asks only:

1. **Industry** — which pack.
2. **Country and city** — sources for that country, one keyword "<city> construction".
3. **3–5 competitors** — company names as people write them. They go to the Keywords sheet (searched every run) and to
   the Players sheet. INTERNAL: competitor names never go into posts or external documents.

```
python3 scripts/industry_pack.py list
python3 scripts/industry_pack.py show construction
python3 scripts/industry_pack.py apply construction --country LV --city Rīga --competitor "Name 1" --competitor "Name 2" --dry
python3 scripts/industry_pack.py apply construction --country LV --city Rīga --competitor "Name 1" --competitor "Name 2"
```

`apply` adds, never overwrites: rows already in the radar stay, the same keyword is never added twice, so it is safe
to run again. A working language the pack does not have (e.g. DE) gets an empty cell and the comment "translate DE" —
the AI assistant translates those rows with the person.

## What a pack adds

| Sheet | What |
|---|---|
| Keywords | the pack's words (ID `BU..`), the city (`Place`), competitors (`CO..`) |
| Sources | typical public sources of the industry for the chosen country and the EU (access "check" until the first run) |
